findings.text: window.STATE_DERIVED_READY is assigned only on the index path — the sole assignment is inside the `if (indexRows !== null)` branch at state-loader.js:395 — while the being-reviewed run's own invariant (state-loader.js:12) is that the page resolves window.STATE_DERIVED_READY after the merge. On the fallback path (index 404 or a refused request) the name is never defined, and that is exactly the path a static build or an index-less deployment takes. A consumer that awaits window.STATE_DERIVED_READY on such a page (await undefined) never resolves, even though the fallback already carries the derived state in its first paint — so the promise should be resolved immediately (or STATE_DERIVED_READY should be set to Promise.resolve(window.STATE)) on both paths. No consumer awaits it yet, so the defect is latent rather than live.

mergeDerived pushes a discovery-only row into state.inventory (state-loader.js:335) and simultaneously records it as pending in state.arrival, so a row the index did not carry is inserted into the list on screen at the moment discovery arrives — contradicting the file's own stated invariant one line above (state-loader.js:321: \"a row the index did not carry is held as an arrival rather than inserted\") and the assemble() path, which holds such rows as pending without inserting them; the plan's 'without re-sorting a list the reader is looking at' is honoured only because the row is appended at the tail. This branch is reachable when a document is created between the index read and the discovery read (a live race), and no test covers it: the second case's discovery payload carries a subset of the index rows (the figure is index-only) and never an extra row, so a regression here would fail no assertion.

justifications.durability: the tests are deterministic — fixed fixture dates, a private basetemp per pytest process, a real server on port 0 with a temp docs tree and a temp config home, no date-derived literal and no state outside the repository under test — and the negative control is bounded by a READY_TIMEOUT_MS so a non-resolving readiness fails rather than stalls. The deduction is the STATE_DERIVED_READY asymmetry (see finding): it is assigned only on the index path, so a page whose index 404'd leaves the name undefined, and the discovery-only-row branch of mergeDerived (the one path a live index/discovery race can reach) is unasserted.
justifications.evidence: the measure is genuine and guarded, and I reproduced the crux myself: the head file at 5340e028e runs green (8 passed, EXIT=0, reviewer-head-crux.log) and the declared negative control reproduces on a scratch copy (readiness gated on window.STATE_DERIVED_READY: the first case fails on its timeout and the second on a first paint that already carries the ready set; 2 loader cases fail, EXIT=1, reviewer-negative-control.log). The first case carries a positive control for its own central assertion — requested_after == [/_index, /_discover] proves the background fetch is deferred past readiness rather than skipped (test file, test_readiness_paints_from_the_index_while_discovery_is_outstanding) — and the second asserts row identity (same_rows) as well as order (keys unchanged), so a merge that rebuilt the list would fail. The base and head gate logs reconcile with the manifest (base-arm-4bdf93dde.log 75 passed 2 skipped EXIT=0; head-arm-39d09daab.log 79 passed 2 skipped EXIT=0). The deduction is that the merge's discovery-only-row branch is the one behaviour with no assertion behind it.
justifications.fit: the moved and added symbols are named by mechanism — canonicalType, isArchivedArtifact, mapLegacyCapability, mapInventoryRow, attachmentRelationsOf, augmentSprints, derivedBlocks, projectRows, assemble, mergeDerived — with header comments that state why the index is the first paint and why the derived payload is merged rather than derived in the browser; no plan, phase, ticket or version label appears in code, symbol or comment, and there is no author attribute. The one deduction is a cosmetic regression: the file now ends without a trailing newline (state-loader.js:571); the \"imas-efit\" and \"north-star\" mentions in comments are pre-existing product/example references, not self-attribution.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §4 asks docs/ui/state-loader.js to fetch /_index/<project> first, render the rows and resolve the page's first paint on it, then fetch /_discover/<project> in the background and merge the derived fields (effective status and the ready set) into the rows already on screen without re-sorting, with the plan body fetched only when a plan is opened and the derived values computed in Python. The loader does exactly this — the index path returns state as soon as /_index answers (state-loader.js:392-407), the discovery fetch is deferred one task later and mergeDerived (state-loader.js:323) Object.assigns each discovery row onto the row of the same nav_key in place (state-loader.js:333) and rebuilds only the derived blocks around it — and the added fallback (index 404 or a refused request takes the old discovery path) is the done-when's own required addition. The deduction is the merge's handling of a discovery-only row (see finding), which inserts rather than defers.
justifications.scope_discipline: `git diff --numstat 4bdf93dde 5340e028e` lists five changed files — docs/evidence/fragments/the-page-paints-from-an-index/page-paints-from-the-index.html (103), docs/ui/state-loader.js (343/226), reckon/serve.py (4/17), tests/test_page_paints_from_the_index.py (497), tests/test_served_loader_reads_discovery_only.py (11/10) — every one inside the node's seven declared write paths; the reviewer's own tree is untouched, no plan or index state was edited, and tests/test_served_loader_reads_discovery_only.py changes only its module docstring (its assertions are byte-identical to base, matching the manifest's claim).
